name: cmu-delphi/covidcast
what_it_is: A collection of R and Python client libraries for Delphi's COVIDcast Epidata API, providing access to daily-updated COVID-19 indicators (cases, deaths, symptom surveys, claims data, mobility) across US geographic regions. Also includes R packages for forecast model building and probabilistic forecast evaluation.
components: covidcast Python package (API client + choropleth/bubble map plotting + geo utilities)
covidcast R package (API client + ggplot2 maps + signal processing) — DEPRECATED, replaced by epidatr
modeltools R package (forecasting and hotspot prediction model tools)
evalcast R package (probabilistic forecaster evaluation with backfill-aware backtesting)
measurement: signal value (confirmed cases, deaths, symptom survey CLI, claims-based ILI, mobility, etc.)
lag (days between time_value and issue date)
configuration: data_source: selects which COVIDcast data source to query
signal: selects which indicator within a source
geo_type: geographic aggregation level (county, state, msa, hrr, dma, hhs, nation)
geo_values: specific geographies or wildcard for all
as_of: retrieve data as it was known on a specific past date
issues: retrieve data published within a specific issue date range
lag: retrieve data published exactly N days after time_value
API key to remove anonymous rate limits
modes: authenticated access (API key, no rate limit on parameter counts)
issue-range data retrieval (all updates within a date window)
constraints: API enforces a maximum result row limit per query; results beyond the limit are silently truncated
Anonymous access is rate-limited and restricted to at most two multi-valued query parameters
R covidcast package is officially deprecated; replacement is the separate epidatr package
Geographic coverage is United States only; no international geographies
evalcast backfill-aware evaluation requires as-of capability; naive backtesting on backfilled data produces overly optimistic scores
notable_absences: No data ingestion or indicator computation (handled by separate covidcast-indicators repo)
No API server or database (handled by separate delphi-epidata repo)
No real-time streaming; all access is batch pull via REST
No built-in forecasting models (modeltools provides building blocks, not finished models)
No CLI tooling; library use only
